**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part:** Banana fruit tip (distal end of a green banana)
- **Key features:**
  - The tip of the banana is showing dark brown to black necrotic rot starting from the blossom end
  - The rot has a dry, shriveled, mummified appearance — wrinkled and collapsed tissue
  - The necrosis progresses from the tip inward, with a sharp transition from healthy green/yellow tissue to the darkened rotted area
  - The texture is dry and fibrous, not wet/mushy
  - The surrounding bananas are otherwise healthy and green

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Anthracnose** — affects banana skin with dark sunken lesions, typically on ripe fruit; can cause tip rot but usually appears as dark spots on yellowing fruit.
- **Bunchy Top** — viral disease affecting the whole plant (stunted growth, bunched leaves); not a fruit tip rot.
- **Cigar End Rot** — classic blossom-end rot of banana fruit caused by *Verticillium* or *Trachysphaera* fungi; produces a dry, dark, mummified rot starting at the tip of the finger, resembling the ash end of a cigar. This matches perfectly.
- **Cordana Leaf Spot** — affects leaves with oval brown spots; not a fruit disease.
- **Panama Disease** — vascular wilt affecting the whole plant from roots upward; not a fruit tip rot.
- **Yellow And Black Sigatoka** — leaf diseases causing yellow/brown streaks on leaves; not fruit tip rot.

The image clearly shows a **dry, dark, mummified rot at the blossom (tip) end of a banana finger**, which is the hallmark symptom of **Cigar End Rot**.
